learning_goals: Explain the mechanism in everyday language and connect it to natural selection, selection pressure, and relative fitness.
Use evidence without demanding exact ratios or a fixed order of concepts.
answer_guidance: Before treatment there is heritable variation in resistance. Under antibiotic exposure, resistant bacteria have greater survival and reproductive success (higher relative fitness). The antibiotic is a selection pressure. Descendants inherit resistance, increasing its frequency. This is natural selection. Do not infer that all susceptible bacteria died or that longer treatment guarantees cure.
completion_guidance: Use holistic judgment. Once the mechanism and relevant scientific concepts have been meaningfully connected, invite the final explanation. A strong initial explanation should move to relevant conceptual extension, not repeated table reading. Do not require a separate answer for every point or exact wording. Students may stop without a claim of mastery.

criteria.description: Identifies natural selection as the process
criteria.credit_guidance: Names natural selection and connects it to their mechanism. Naming alone without understanding is partial evidence.

criteria.description: Identifies the antibiotic as the selection pressure
criteria.credit_guidance: Accept equivalent language explaining the antibiotic as the environmental factor causing differential success. Define an unfamiliar term without identifying its case-specific answer.

criteria.description: Selection acts on existing heritable variation
criteria.credit_guidance: Combine statements across turns. Pre-existing resistant bacteria plus inherited resistance is sufficient. Do not repeatedly require explaining the existence of two categories.

criteria.description: Connects differential survival and reproductive success to fitness during treatment
criteria.credit_guidance: Credit the survival/reproduction reasoning in everyday language. Develop the connection to relative fitness if needed. Fitness is context-dependent, not strength or survival alone.

criteria.description: Explains why inherited resistance becomes more frequent
criteria.credit_guidance: Survivors produce resistant descendants, increasing their share. Exact ratios and population sizes are not required.

common_misconceptions: Antibiotics intentionally cause mutations bacteria need.
Every susceptible bacterium must turn resistant for the population to change.
Fitness means strongest regardless of environment and reproductive success.
The samples track the same 100 individual bacteria.
teaching_notes: Do not infer a misconception from a short or colloquial answer. Ask only if ambiguity matters.
An initial explanation that susceptible bacteria die and resistant bacteria reproduce captures important mechanistic reasoning. Build on it by inviting connection to evolutionary concepts.
Definitions are allowed; leave their case-specific application to the student unless explicitly requested.
